title: Spec Kit portable package snapshot inventory (SNAPSHOT.json)
description: Self-describing inventory of every delivered package file except SNAPSHOT.json itself and the completion marker SNAPSHOT.json.sha256. Serialized as UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings, one trailing newline, files sorted ascending by path. The inventory cannot contain its own hash; that digest lives in the completion marker and is recorded out of band.

schema_version.description: Snapshot inventory schema version. Distinct from the installer's consumer install-manifest schema; the two records have different trust roles.

label.description: Human-readable snapshot name. Uniqueness across snapshots is a human convention documented in the package README; it is not enforced by tooling or this schema (no registry exists). Attaches to an assembled result only when the completion marker exists and inventory comparison passes. Printable characters only (no control characters), bounded length.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 capture timestamp with UTC offset.

captured_by.description: Capturing human / invocation reference. The referenced human snapshot approval authorizes capture of uncommitted working-tree content. Printable characters only (no control characters), bounded length.

source_reference.description: Reference only, not a fidelity claim: the working tree may differ from the commit; packaged bytes are authoritative via per-file digests.

bundle_version.description: bundle_version of scripts/speckit-portable-bundle.json at capture (1.1.0 at planning time).

digest_algorithm.description: Declared (not assumed) per-file digest algorithm for schema_version 1.

files.description: Sorted ascending by path; duplicate paths invalid; casefolded ancestor/descendant collisions invalid (Windows-safe uniqueness).

path.description: Package-relative POSIX path. The pattern rejects absolute paths, empty segments (e.g. 'a//b'), '.'/'..' segments, forbidden characters (backslash : < > " | ? * NUL) and segments ending in a dot or space. Caveat: schema validation is advisory — procedural validation per the installer's _relative_path rules is authoritative; in particular the pattern does not encode Windows reserved device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9), which are rejected procedurally.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 over raw bytes (binary mode).

origin.description: source = captured allowlist file or packaging entry point (package path equals source-relative path); package-doc = package-only documentation/metadata.

source_path.description: In-repo authoring path; present only for package-doc entries whose package path differs from the source path.
